title: Zobeide
summary: A book that refuses to stay a book. Calvino’s text cut into strips and rebuilt as the maze it describes.
coverAlt: White paper strips printed with text, stacked into a tangled structure

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body: Turn your city into a book. The format is open, but the text has to stay readable somewhere.

blocks.heading: The city
blocks.body: Zobeide was built by men who all dreamed of the same woman running through a city at night. They built streets to trap her, and she never came back. The city is a trap made out of a dream.

blocks.label: Dummy books. Photos of the first two conventional bound versions, before the strip idea.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body:
I set the passage as one long line of type, printed it on heavy stock and cut it into sticks. Each stick carries a fragment.

Stacked together they form a structure your eyes can wander through but never read in order, the same way the men of Zobeide walk streets that lead nowhere.

blocks.label: Cutting and assembly. Two or three photos of the strips being cut and joined.

blocks.alt: Close-up of a paper strip reading spot where they had lost the fugitive’s trail
blocks.caption: Fragments stay readable up close.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body:
My first two dummies were good books with weak ideas. The breakthrough came when I stopped protecting the format.

Photography became part of the design. The lighting decides which words a viewer finds first.
